fatal_errors: The proposed Si addition and oxidation treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention, which varies Mo content in a CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
None of the cited evidence establishes that 2–3 at.% Si and oxidation at 850 °C produce a continuous, self-healing amorphous SiO2 film on this alloy.
The description of SiO2 as a lubricious, low-shear tribofilm is unsupported by the cited passages and is not generally justified without direct phase, structure, and tribological evidence.
The predicted 40% friction and 50% wear reductions are invented quantitative values with no supporting baseline data.
The intervention combines alloying and heat treatment without factorial controls, so the proposed experiment cannot attribute any benefit specifically to Si addition or oxidation.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad problem of wide-temperature HEA tribology and provides a testable treated-versus-control experiment, measurements, limitations, and explicit falsification thresholds. However, it is scientifically remote from the hidden target: it changes the alloy system, omits the MoS2/Ag/Cr2O3 self-lubricating composite, replaces Mo-driven lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening with speculative silica formation, and does not reproduce the specified SPS or tribological conditions. The only mechanistic overlap is the generic idea that an oxide-derived surface film may protect at elevated temperature. The cited evidence supports tribolayers and temperature-dependent oxide coverage only in general; it does not support selective silica-film formation, low shear strength, self-healing behavior, the processing window, or the numerical performance claims. The experiment is reasonably falsifiable but lacks exact load, speed, counterface, atmosphere, and distance, and should include Si-only, oxidation-only, and untreated controls.
